policy: One finding per commit; one push after the final commit. GitHub Actions remain disabled.

findings.title: [P1] Serialize saves across preview sessions
findings.body: Two previews of the same JSON can both pass the final source-hash check before either rename, so one save overwrites the other. Both helper calls succeeded in all 20 reproduction trials; concurrent preview API requests also overwrote one edit and returned a rebuild error instead of a conflict. The save queue belongs to each server instance. Hold a shared source-file lock across the hash check and atomic replacement, then reject the losing save with 409 before modifying the source.
findings.change: Guard canonical JSON sources with the existing cross-process artifact lock across conflict checks and atomic replacement.
findings.validation: Red: helper saves both succeeded and independent preview returned 422. Green: all 6 save tests pass, including independent previews, repeated helper races and separate Node processes.

findings.title: [P2] Restore focus after keyboard handle edits
findings.body: Each arrow adjustment submits an accepted edit and rebuilds the graph, removing its focused SVG handle. In the browser, ArrowRight moved focus from the handle to BODY, and a second ArrowRight did not change the curve. Preserve or restore the selected handle focus after acceptance so repeated keyboard adjustment works, as required by the inspector keyboard-access standard in .impeccable.md.
findings.change: Restore the selected SVG handle focus after accepted keyboard edits; pointer edits retain their existing behavior.
findings.validation: Red: the repeated-keyboard browser test lost focus after its first adjustment. Green: inspector acceptance passes with consecutive horizontal and Shift vertical edits, undo, save, phone layout and native MP4 parity.

findings.title: [P2] Preserve structured validation diagnostics
findings.body: This collapses native validateComposition diagnostics into one string. The save API then substitutes a generic code and the source filename for the original codes and JSON paths, and omits severity; both export APIs return plain text. Preserve the original diagnostic objects and return the structured envelope required by docs/composition-engine-plan.md engineering invariant 7.
findings.change: Retain native validation and font diagnostics through the shared passage-diagnostics error model; save and both export APIs return JSON envelopes, and the Lab displays their property paths.
findings.validation: Red: save flattened two native range errors into one generic filename diagnostic. Green: all 7 save/API tests pass; invalid documents return the exact native diagnostics from save and both export endpoints. TypeScript build passes.

findings.title: [P2] Preserve the opposite side when editing a handle
findings.body: Deleting the selected key smoothing settings changes both adjacent segments. For rotation keys (0,0), (10,10,smooth:true), (20,40), applying only an outgoing handle with ease 0.6 and speed 2 changes frame 5 from 2.5 to 5, even though frame 5 belongs to the incoming segment. The native sampler supports an explicit outgoing handle with smooth incoming motion. Preserve the opposite side when replacing one handle.
findings.change: Keep shared smooth settings when replacing one temporal handle so the opposite segment retains its native motion.
findings.validation: Red: both smooth encodings changed untouched incoming values (frame 5: 2.5 to 5). Green: 13 curve/history tests pass with exact incoming/outgoing preservation, edited-side changes and undo/redo round trips.

findings.title: [P2] Clear stale copied code when selecting path keys
findings.body: This early return runs before updating the edited-key code field and copy action. After selecting a keyed mask path following rotation, the title names masks[cutout].path but Copy edited keys still copies transform.rotation and its keys. The no-track branch has the same stale state. Update or clear the code field and disable copying where no valid snippet is available before returning.
findings.change: Reset copy state on every graph selection, populate native path-key snippets before the numeric-graph early return, and disable copying when the source has no tracks.
findings.validation: Red: selecting masks[cutout].path retained transform.position code. Green: inspector acceptance passes path snippet selection and empty-source copy disabling alongside editing, watch, phone and MP4 parity checks.

findings.title: [P2] Discover separated constraint-reference channels
findings.body: constraintReference is passed to add as one vector, so separated x/y animations are skipped. A valid solid layer with constraintReference: { x: { keys: [{ frame: 0, value: 0 }, { frame: 20, value: 20 }] }, y: 0 } produces zero tracks. Visit the separated channels as transform vectors do so these native property paths have the required key lanes and graphs.
findings.change: Discover separated x/y channels through one native vector-track path, including constraintReference, with scalar lanes, resolved graphs, edits and code copies.
findings.validation: Red: valid separated constraintReference returned no tracks. Green: all 10 key tests and inspector acceptance pass, including native reference path sampling, handle edits, code copy and history. TypeScript build passes.

findings.title: [P3] Share curve sampling and speed calculation
findings.body: Possible Duplicated Code (judgement call): this resolved-graph sampler and composition-keys.ts:293-306 both sample a curve uniformly and calculate speeds from clipped plus/minus 0.01 finite differences. A shared sampler accepting the range, sample count and evaluator would keep authored and resolved graphs consistent when derivative behavior changes. This is a maintainability concern rather than a documented-standard violation.
